questions.question: Poochie can type 600 words in 5 minutes less than Katie. If Poochie types at a rate of 20 words per minute faster than Katie, what is Poochie's typing rate?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Words to type = 600 words
• Poochie is 20 words/min faster than Katie
• Poochie takes 5 minutes less

Let Katie's rate be x words/min. Poochie's rate is x + 20.

Formula:
Time = Words / Rate

Solution:
600/x - 600/(x + 20) = 5

600(x + 20) - 600x = 5x(x + 20)
12000 = 5x² + 100x
x² + 20x - 2400 = 0

Factoring:
(x + 60)(x - 40) = 0

Thus Katie = 40 words/min.
Poochie = 40 + 20 = 60 words/min.

Therefore, Poochie's typing rate is 60 words/min.

questions.question: An aircraft flies 120 km east and then 50 km north. What is its straight-line displacement from the starting point?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Eastward displacement = 120 km
• Northward displacement = 50 km

Formula:
R = √(x² + y²)

Solution:
R = √(120² + 50²)
R = √(14400 + 2500)
R = √16900
R = 130 km

Therefore, the straight-line displacement is 130 km.

questions.question: An aircraft travels 200 km on a bearing of 060°. What are the approximate north and east components of its displacement?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Distance = 200 km
• Bearing = 060°

For a bearing measured clockwise from north:
North component = R cos θ
East component = R sin θ

Solution:
North = 200 cos 60° = 200(0.5) = 100 km
East = 200 sin 60° = 200(0.866) = 173.2 km

Therefore, the displacement components are 100 km north and 173.2 km east.

questions.question: Two aircraft positions relative to an airport are A = 80 km east and B = 60 km north. What is the bearing of B from A?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• A is 80 km east of the airport.
• B is 60 km north of the airport.

From A to B:
• North component = 60 km
• West component = 80 km

Formula:
tan θ = opposite / adjacent

Solution:
tan θ = 80/60
θ = arctan(80/60)
θ ≈ 53.1°

The direction is north-west, so the bearing is:
360° - 53.1° = 306.9°

Therefore, the bearing is 306.9°.

questions.question: A projectile is launched horizontally from a 45 m high cliff at 20 m/s. Neglecting air resistance, how long does it take to hit the ground? Use g = 9.8 m/s².
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Vertical displacement = 45 m
• Initial vertical velocity = 0
• g = 9.8 m/s²

Formula:
y = v₀t + (1/2)gt²

Solution:
45 = 0 + 4.9t²
t² = 45/4.9
t = √(9.1837)
t ≈ 3.03 s

The horizontal velocity does not affect the time of fall because horizontal and vertical motions are independent.

Therefore, the projectile hits the ground after approximately 3.03 s.

questions.question: A projectile is launched at 30 m/s at an angle of 40° above the horizontal. Using g = 9.8 m/s², what is its maximum height above the launch point?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Initial velocity = 30 m/s
• θ = 40°
• g = 9.8 m/s²

First find the vertical component:
v₀y = v₀ sin θ
v₀y = 30 sin 40° ≈ 19.28 m/s

Formula:
H = v₀y²/(2g)

Solution:
H = (19.28)²/(2(9.8))
H ≈ 371.7/19.6
H ≈ 18.97 m

Therefore, the maximum height is approximately 18.97 m.

questions.question: A rectangular open-top tank has length 6 m, width 4 m, and water depth 3 m. What is the volume of water?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Length = 6 m
• Width = 4 m
• Depth = 3 m

Formula:
V = lwh

Solution:
V = (6)(4)(3)
V = 72 m³

Therefore, the volume of water is 72 m³.

questions.question: A cylindrical tank has radius 2 m and height 5 m. What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
Given:
• Radius r = 2 m
• Height h = 5 m

Formula:
V = πr²h

Solution:
V = π(2²)(5)
V = π(4)(5)
V = 20π m³

Therefore, the cylinder volume is 20π m³.

questions.question: Solve for x: log₂(x) = 5.
questions.explanation:
Given:
log₂(x) = 5

Formula:
log_b(x) = y means x = b^y.

Solution:
x = 2⁵
x = 32

Therefore, x = 32.

questions.question: Solve for x: ln(x) + ln(4) = ln(20).
questions.explanation:
Given:
ln(x) + ln(4) = ln(20)

Formula:
ln a + ln b = ln(ab)

Solution:
ln(4x) = ln(20)
4x = 20
x = 5

Therefore, x = 5.

questions.question: The position of an aircraft along a runway is given by s(t) = 4t³ + 2t². What is its velocity at t = 2 s?
questions.explanation:
Given:
s(t) = 4t³ + 2t²

t = 2 s

Formula:
v(t) = ds/dt

Solution:
v(t) = 12t² + 4t
v(2) = 12(2²) + 4(2)
v(2) = 48 + 8
v(2) = 56 m/s

Therefore, the velocity is 56 m/s.

questions.question: The radius of a circular object increases at 2 cm/s. At the instant r = 5 cm, how fast is its area increasing?
questions.explanation:
Given:
dr/dt = 2 cm/s
r = 5 cm

Formula:
A = πr²
Differentiate:
dA/dt = 2πr(dr/dt)

Solution:
dA/dt = 2π(5)(2)
dA/dt = 20π cm²/s

Therefore, the area is increasing at 20π cm²/s.

questions.question: A father is 4 times as old as his son. In 12 years, the father will be twice as old as his son. How old is the son now?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Father's age = 4x
Son's age = x

In 12 years:
Father = 4x + 12
Son = x + 12

Equation:
4x + 12 = 2(x + 12)

Solution:
4x + 12 = 2x + 24
2x = 12
x = 6

Therefore, the son is 6 years old.

questions.question: A force of 50 N moves an object 8 m in the direction of the force. What work is done?
questions.explanation:
Given:
F = 50 N
d = 8 m

Formula:
W = Fd

Solution:
W = (50)(8)
W = 400 J

Therefore, the work done is 400 J.

questions.question: A variable force is given by F(x) = 4x² N. Find the work done from x = 0 to x = 3 m.
questions.explanation:
Given:
F(x) = 4x² N
x = 0 to 3 m

Formula:
W = ∫ F(x) dx

Solution:
W = ∫₀³ 4x² dx
W = 4[x³/3]₀³
W = 4(27/3)
W = 36 J

Therefore, the work is 36 J.

questions.question: A steel bar is 2 m long and experiences a temperature increase of 50°C. If α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C, what is its free thermal expansion?
questions.explanation:
Given:
L = 2 m
ΔT = 50°C
α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C

Formula:
ΔL = αLΔT

Solution:
ΔL = (12 × 10⁻⁶)(2)(50)
ΔL = 1200 × 10⁻⁶
ΔL = 0.0012 m

Therefore, the free thermal expansion is 0.0012 m, or 1.2 mm.

questions.question: A steel bar is completely restrained from expanding. If E = 200 GPa and α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C, what thermal stress develops for a temperature increase of 40°C?
questions.explanation:
Given:
E = 200 GPa
α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C
ΔT = 40°C

For complete restraint, thermal stress magnitude is:
σ = EαΔT

Solution:
σ = (200 × 10⁹)(12 × 10⁻⁶)(40)
σ = 96 × 10⁶ Pa
σ = 96 MPa

Because the bar wants to expand but is restrained, the stress is compressive.

Therefore, the thermal stress magnitude is 96 MPa compressive.

questions.question: An ideal gas has pressure 200 kPa, volume 0.5 m³, and temperature 300 K. What is its amount in moles? Use R = 8.314 J/(mol·K).
questions.explanation:
Given:
P = 200 kPa = 200,000 Pa
V = 0.5 m³
T = 300 K
R = 8.314 J/(mol·K)

Formula:
PV = nRT

Solve for n:
n = PV/(RT)

Solution:
n = (200000)(0.5)/(8.314)(300)
n = 100000/2494.2
n ≈ 40.09 mol

Therefore, the amount of gas is approximately 40.09 mol.

questions.question: An ideal gas occupies 2 m³ at 100 kPa and 300 K. If its temperature increases to 450 K at constant pressure, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation:
Given:
P is constant
V₁ = 2 m³
T₁ = 300 K
T₂ = 450 K

At constant pressure, Charles' law gives:
V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂

Solution:
V₂ = V₁(T₂/T₁)
V₂ = 2(450/300)
V₂ = 3 m³

Therefore, the new volume is 3.00 m³.

questions.question: A dataset is 2, 4, 4, 6, and 9. What is its population standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Data = 2, 4, 4, 6, 9

Formula:
σ = √[Σ(x - μ)²/n]

Mean:
μ = (2 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 9)/5 = 25/5 = 5

Squared deviations:
9, 1, 1, 1, 16
Sum = 28

Variance:
28/5 = 5.6

Standard deviation:
σ = √5.6 ≈ 2.37

Therefore, the population standard deviation is approximately 2.37. Note that none of the listed choices matches this value, indicating that the choices contain an error.

questions.question: A wheel rotates at 120 revolutions per minute. What is its angular velocity in rad/s?
questions.explanation:
Given:
120 rpm

Formula:
ω = revolutions × 2π radians / time

Solution:
120 rev/min × (2π rad/rev) × (1 min/60 s)
= 240π/60
= 4π rad/s

Therefore, the angular velocity is 4π rad/s.

questions.question: A 2 m radius wheel rotates at 5 rad/s. What is the tangential velocity of a point on its rim?
questions.explanation:
Given:
r = 2 m
ω = 5 rad/s

Formula:
v = rω

Solution:
v = (2)(5)
v = 10 m/s

Therefore, the tangential velocity is 10 m/s.

questions.question: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30° above horizontal. What is its horizontal range if it lands at the same elevation? Use g = 9.8 m/s².
questions.explanation:
Given:
v₀ = 20 m/s
θ = 30°
g = 9.8 m/s²

Formula:
R = v₀² sin(2θ)/g

Solution:
R = 20² sin(60°)/9.8
R = 400(0.8660)/9.8
R ≈ 35.35 m

Therefore, the horizontal range is approximately 35.35 m.

questions.question: A bearing of 135° corresponds to which general direction?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Bearing = 135°

Bearings are measured clockwise from north.
0° = North
90° = East
180° = South
270° = West

Since 135° lies halfway between 90° and 180°, it points southeast.

Therefore, the direction is southeast.

questions.question: An aircraft travels 150 km north and then 200 km east. What is the magnitude of the resultant displacement?
questions.explanation:
Given:
North = 150 km
East = 200 km

Formula:
R = √(N² + E²)

Solution:
R = √(150² + 200²)
R = √(22500 + 40000)
R = √62500
R = 250 km

Therefore, the resultant displacement is 250 km.

questions.question: A car's position is s(t) = t³ - 6t² + 9t. At what times is its velocity zero?
questions.explanation:
Given:
s(t) = t³ - 6t² + 9t

Formula:
v(t) = ds/dt

Solution:
v(t) = 3t² - 12t + 9
Set velocity equal to zero:
3t² - 12t + 9 = 0
Divide by 3:
t² - 4t + 3 = 0
(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0

Therefore:
t = 1 s or t = 3 s.

questions.question: A rectangle has perimeter 40 m. What dimensions give the maximum area?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Perimeter = 40 m

Let width = x and length = y.

Formula:
2x + 2y = 40
x + y = 20

y = 20 - x

Area:
A = xy
A(x) = x(20 - x)
A(x) = 20x - x²

Differentiate:
A'(x) = 20 - 2x

Set equal to zero:
20 - 2x = 0
x = 10

y = 20 - 10 = 10

Therefore, the maximum-area rectangle is 10 m × 10 m.

questions.question: A rectangular box has a square base and no top. It must have a volume of 32 m³. What base side length minimizes the surface area?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Volume = 32 m³
Square base side = x
Height = h

Formula:
V = x²h

Therefore:
h = 32/x²

Surface area without a top:
S = x² + 4xh

Substitute h:
S = x² + 4x(32/x²)
S = x² + 128/x

Differentiate:
S' = 2x - 128/x²

Set equal to zero:
2x = 128/x²
2x³ = 128
x³ = 64
x = 4 m

Therefore, the base side that minimizes surface area is 4 m.

questions.question: A water tank has a horizontal area of 5 m² and is 4 m deep. How much work is required to pump all the water to the top? Use γ = 9800 N/m³.
questions.explanation:
Given:
A = 5 m²
Depth = 4 m
γ = 9800 N/m³

For a slice at height y:
dV = 5dy
Weight = 9800(5dy)
Distance to top = 4 - y

Formula:
W = ∫ γA(4-y)dy

Solution:
W = ∫₀⁴ 9800(5)(4-y)dy
W = 49000[4y - y²/2]₀⁴
W = 49000(16 - 8)
W = 49000(8)
W = 392000 J

Therefore, the required work is 392000 J.

questions.question: A vertical rectangular plate is 2 m wide and 4 m high. Its top is 1 m below the water surface. What is the hydrostatic force? Use γ = 9800 N/m³.
questions.explanation:
Given:
Width = 2 m
Height = 4 m
Top depth = 1 m
Bottom depth = 5 m
γ = 9800 N/m³

Use average depth:
h_avg = (1 + 5)/2 = 3 m

Area:
A = 2(4) = 8 m²

Formula:
F = γh_avgA

Solution:
F = 9800(3)(8)
F = 235200 N

Therefore, the hydrostatic force is 235200 N. The listed choices do not contain the correct value, so the choices contain an error.

questions.question: A rod is 4 m long with linear density ρ(x) = 3 + x kg/m. What is its total mass?
questions.explanation:
Given:
ρ(x) = 3 + x kg/m
0 ≤ x ≤ 4

Formula:
dm = ρ(x)dx
m = ∫ρ(x)dx

Solution:
m = ∫₀⁴(3+x)dx
m = [3x + x²/2]₀⁴
m = 12 + 8
m = 20 kg

Therefore, the rod's total mass is 20 kg.

questions.question: A particle has velocity v(t) = 3t² - 4t + 2 m/s. What is its acceleration at t = 2 s?
questions.explanation:
Given:
v(t) = 3t² - 4t + 2

t = 2 s

Formula:
a(t) = dv/dt

Solution:
a(t) = 6t - 4
a(2) = 12 - 4
 a(2) = 8 m/s²

Therefore, the acceleration is 8 m/s².

questions.question: The radius of a sphere increases at 0.5 m/s. At r = 2 m, how fast is its volume increasing?
questions.explanation:
Given:
dr/dt = 0.5 m/s
r = 2 m

Formula:
V = (4/3)πr³

Differentiate:
dV/dt = 4πr²(dr/dt)

Solution:
dV/dt = 4π(2²)(0.5)
dV/dt = 4π(4)(0.5)
dV/dt = 8π m³/s

Therefore, the volume increases at 8π m³/s.

questions.question: A father is 30 years older than his son. In 5 years, the father will be three times as old as his son. How old is the son now?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Father = Son + 30
Let son = x.
Father = x + 30.

In 5 years:
Father = x + 35
Son = x + 5

Formula:
x + 35 = 3(x + 5)

Solution:
x + 35 = 3x + 15
20 = 2x
x = 10

Therefore, the son is 10 years old.

questions.question: A force varies with position as F(x) = 10 - 2x N. What is the work done from x = 0 to x = 4 m?
questions.explanation:
Given:
F(x) = 10 - 2x
x = 0 to 4 m

Formula:
W = ∫₀⁴F(x)dx

Solution:
W = ∫₀⁴(10 - 2x)dx
W = [10x - x²]₀⁴
W = 40 - 16
W = 24 J

Therefore, the work done is 24 J.

questions.question: An aluminum rod has α = 23 × 10⁻⁶/°C and is 3 m long. What is its expansion for a temperature increase of 80°C?
questions.explanation:
Given:
α = 23 × 10⁻⁶/°C
L = 3 m
ΔT = 80°C

Formula:
ΔL = αLΔT

Solution:
ΔL = (23 × 10⁻⁶)(3)(80)
ΔL = 5520 × 10⁻⁶
ΔL = 0.00552 m

Therefore, the expansion is 0.00552 m, or 5.52 mm.

questions.question: A gas occupies 0.8 m³ at 150 kPa and 300 K. What volume will it occupy at 100 kPa and 400 K, assuming the amount of gas is constant?
questions.explanation:
Given:
P₁ = 150 kPa
V₁ = 0.8 m³
T₁ = 300 K
P₂ = 100 kPa
T₂ = 400 K

Formula:
P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂

Solve:
V₂ = P₁V₁T₂/(T₁P₂)

Solution:
V₂ = (150)(0.8)(400)/(300)(100)
V₂ = 48000/30000
V₂ = 1.6 m³

Therefore, the new volume is 1.60 m³.

questions.question: For the data 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, what is the standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Given:
All observations are 5.

Formula:
σ = √[Σ(x - μ)²/n]

Mean:
μ = 5

Every deviation is:
x - μ = 5 - 5 = 0

Therefore:
σ = √(0) = 0

All values are identical, so there is no spread.

questions.question: An aircraft propeller rotates at 1800 rpm. What is its angular velocity in rad/s?
questions.explanation:
Given:
1800 rpm

Formula:
ω = rpm × 2π/60

Solution:
ω = 1800(2π)/60
ω = 30(2π)
ω = 60π rad/s

Therefore, the angular velocity is 60π rad/s.

questions.question: A projectile is launched vertically upward at 49 m/s. Using g = 9.8 m/s², what maximum height does it reach?
questions.explanation:
Given:
v₀ = 49 m/s
g = 9.8 m/s²

At maximum height, final velocity is zero.

Formula:
v² = v₀² - 2gH

Set v = 0:
0 = 49² - 2(9.8)H

Solution:
H = 49²/(19.6)
H = 2401/19.6
H = 122.5 m

Therefore, the maximum height is 122.5 m.

questions.question: A ship travels 300 km on a bearing of 120°. What is its eastward component?
questions.explanation:
Given:
R = 300 km
Bearing = 120°

For a bearing measured from north:
East component = R sin θ

Solution:
East = 300 sin 120°
East = 300(0.8660)
East ≈ 259.8 km

Therefore, the eastward component is approximately 259.8 km.

questions.question: A 10 m ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its bottom moves away from the wall at 2 m/s. When the bottom is 6 m from the wall, how fast is the top moving downward?
questions.explanation:
Given:
L = 10 m
x = 6 m
dx/dt = 2 m/s

Relationship:
x² + y² = 10²

Differentiate:
2x dx/dt + 2y dy/dt = 0

Find y:
y = √(100 - 36) = 8 m

Solve:
dy/dt = -(x/y)(dx/dt)

dy/dt = -(6/8)(2)
= -1.5 m/s

The negative sign means downward.
Therefore, the top moves downward at 1.5 m/s.

questions.question: A rectangular field has length x and width 20 - x. What value of x gives maximum area?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Length = x
Width = 20 - x

Formula:
A = lw

Solution:
A(x) = x(20-x)
A(x) = 20x - x²

Differentiate:
A'(x) = 20 - 2x

Set equal to zero:
20 - 2x = 0
x = 10

Second derivative:
A''(x) = -2 < 0
Therefore, this is a maximum.

Thus x = 10.

questions.question: A cylindrical can has radius r and height h. If its volume is fixed at 100π cm³, what is h in terms of r?
questions.explanation:
Given:
V = 100π cm³

Formula:
V = πr²h

Solve for h:
100π = πr²h
Divide by π:
100 = r²h

Therefore:
h = 100/r²

Thus the correct expression is h = 100/r².

questions.question: Evaluate ln(e⁵).
questions.explanation:
Given:
ln(e⁵)

Formula:
ln(e^x) = x

Solution:
ln(e⁵) = 5

Therefore, the answer is 5.

questions.question: The position of a particle is s(t) = 2t³ - 3t² + 4t. What is its acceleration at t = 1 s?
questions.explanation:
Given:
s(t) = 2t³ - 3t² + 4t

Formula:
a(t) = d²s/dt²

First derivative:
v(t) = 6t² - 6t + 4

Second derivative:
a(t) = 12t - 6

At t = 1:
a(1) = 12 - 6 = 6 m/s²

Therefore, the acceleration is 6 m/s².

questions.question: A vertical gate is 4 m wide and 3 m high, with its top 2 m below the water surface. Using γ = 9800 N/m³, what is the hydrostatic force?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Width = 4 m
Height = 3 m
Top depth = 2 m
Bottom depth = 5 m

Average depth:
h_avg = (2+5)/2 = 3.5 m

Area:
A = 4(3) = 12 m²

Formula:
F = γh_avgA

Solution:
F = 9800(3.5)(12)
F = 9800(42)
F = 411600 N

Therefore, the correct force is 411600 N. None of the listed choices matches, indicating an error in the choices.

questions.question: A steel member has an original length of 1.5 m. If its free thermal expansion is 0.9 mm, what is the thermal strain?
questions.explanation:
Given:
ΔL = 0.9 mm = 0.0009 m
L = 1.5 m

Formula:
ε = ΔL/L

Solution:
ε = 0.0009/1.5
ε = 0.0006

Therefore, the thermal strain is 0.0006.

questions.question: A gas has P = 300 kPa, V = 0.2 m³, and T = 400 K. What is the number of moles? Use R = 8.314 J/(mol·K).
questions.explanation:
Given:
P = 300000 Pa
V = 0.2 m³
T = 400 K
R = 8.314 J/(mol·K)

Formula:
PV = nRT
n = PV/(RT)

Solution:
n = (300000)(0.2)/(8.314)(400)
n = 60000/3325.6
n ≈ 18.04 mol

Therefore, the amount of gas is approximately 18.04 mol.

questions.question: The data set is 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18. What is the population standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Data = 10, 12, 14, 16, 18

Mean:
μ = (10+12+14+16+18)/5 = 14

Squared deviations:
16, 4, 0, 4, 16
Sum = 40

Formula:
σ = √(Σ(x-μ)²/n)

Solution:
σ = √(40/5)
σ = √8
σ ≈ 2.83

Therefore, the population standard deviation is approximately 2.83.

questions.question: A rotating disk has angular velocity 12 rad/s and radius 0.5 m. What is the centripetal acceleration at its edge?
questions.explanation:
Given:
ω = 12 rad/s
r = 0.5 m

Formula:
a_c = ω²r

Solution:
a_c = (12²)(0.5)
a_c = 144(0.5)
a_c = 72 m/s²

Therefore, the centripetal acceleration is 72 m/s².

questions.question: A projectile is fired at 50 m/s at 37° above horizontal. Using sin 37° = 0.6 and cos 37° = 0.8, what is its initial vertical velocity?
questions.explanation:
Given:
v₀ = 50 m/s
θ = 37°
sin 37° = 0.6

Formula:
v₀y = v₀ sin θ

Solution:
v₀y = 50(0.6)
v₀y = 30 m/s

Therefore, the initial vertical velocity is 30 m/s.

questions.question: A plane flies 400 km on a bearing of 030°. What is its northward component?
questions.explanation:
Given:
R = 400 km
Bearing = 30°

Formula:
North component = R cos θ

Solution:
North = 400 cos 30°
North = 400(0.8660)
North ≈ 346.4 km

Therefore, the northward component is approximately 346.4 km.

questions.question: A circular tank is being filled so that its radius increases at 0.1 m/s. At r = 3 m, how fast is its area increasing?
questions.explanation:
Given:
dr/dt = 0.1 m/s
r = 3 m

Formula:
A = πr²

Differentiate:
dA/dt = 2πr(dr/dt)

Solution:
dA/dt = 2π(3)(0.1)
dA/dt = 0.6π m²/s

Therefore, the area is increasing at 0.6π m²/s.

questions.question: A 4 m rod has density ρ(x) = 2x kg/m. What is its total mass?
questions.explanation:
Given:
ρ(x) = 2x kg/m
0 ≤ x ≤ 4

Formula:
m = ∫ρ(x)dx

Solution:
m = ∫₀⁴2x dx
m = [x²]₀⁴
m = 16 kg

Therefore, the total mass is 16 kg.

questions.question: A company has revenue R(x) = 80x - x² and cost C(x) = 20x + 100. What production level maximizes profit?
questions.explanation:
Given:
R(x) = 80x - x²
C(x) = 20x + 100

Formula:
P(x) = R(x) - C(x)

Solution:
P(x) = (80x-x²) - (20x+100)
P(x) = -x² + 60x - 100

Differentiate:
P'(x) = -2x + 60

Set equal to zero:
-2x + 60 = 0
x = 30

Second derivative:
P''(x) = -2 < 0

Therefore, the maximum profit occurs at 30 units.

questions.question: A rectangular tank has horizontal water area 6 m² and depth 4 m. Find the work required to pump all water to the top. Use γ = 9800 N/m³.
questions.explanation:
Given:
A = 6 m²
Depth = 4 m
γ = 9800 N/m³

For a thin slice at height y:
dV = 6dy
Weight = 9800(6dy)
Distance to top = 4-y

Formula:
W = ∫₀⁴ γA(4-y)dy

Solution:
W = ∫₀⁴ 9800(6)(4-y)dy
W = 58800[4y-y²/2]₀⁴
W = 58800(8)
W = 470400 J

Therefore, the required work is 470400 J.

questions.question: A vertical square plate has side 2 m and its top is 1 m below the water surface. Using γ = 9800 N/m³, what is the hydrostatic force?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Width = 2 m
Height = 2 m
Top depth = 1 m
Bottom depth = 3 m
γ = 9800 N/m³

Average depth:
h_avg = (1+3)/2 = 2 m

Area:
A = 2(2) = 4 m²

Formula:
F = γh_avgA

Solution:
F = 9800(2)(4)
F = 78400 N

Therefore, the hydrostatic force is 78400 N.

questions.question: A 10 m ladder leans against a wall. If its bottom is 6 m from the wall, what is the height reached by the ladder?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Ladder = 10 m
Horizontal distance = 6 m

Formula:
x² + y² = L²

Solution:
6² + y² = 10²
36 + y² = 100
y² = 64
y = 8 m

Therefore, the ladder reaches 8 m up the wall.

questions.question: A steel bar has E = 200 GPa and thermal expansion coefficient α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C. If completely restrained and heated by 25°C, what thermal stress develops?
questions.explanation:
Given:
E = 200 GPa
α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C
ΔT = 25°C

Formula:
σ = EαΔT

Solution:
σ = (200 × 10⁹)(12 × 10⁻⁶)(25)
σ = 60 × 10⁶ Pa
σ = 60 MPa

The stress is compressive because expansion is restrained.

Therefore, the thermal stress magnitude is 60 MPa.

questions.question: An ideal gas contains 2 mol at 300 K and occupies 0.05 m³. What is its pressure? Use R = 8.314 J/(mol·K).
questions.explanation:
Given:
n = 2 mol
T = 300 K
V = 0.05 m³
R = 8.314 J/(mol·K)

Formula:
PV = nRT
P = nRT/V

Solution:
P = (2)(8.314)(300)/0.05
P = 4988.4/0.05
P = 99768 Pa
P ≈ 99.77 kPa

Therefore, the pressure is approximately 99.77 kPa.

questions.question: A data set has mean 50 and population standard deviation 4. If every value is increased by 10, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Original standard deviation = 4
Every observation is increased by 10.

Rule:
Adding or subtracting a constant from every data value changes the mean but does not change the standard deviation.

Therefore:
New standard deviation = 4

The spread of the data remains exactly the same.

questions.question: A wheel rotates through 20 revolutions in 4 seconds. What is its average angular velocity?
questions.explanation:
Given:
20 revolutions
Time = 4 s

Angular displacement:
θ = 20(2π) = 40π rad

Formula:
ω_avg = θ/t

Solution:
ω_avg = 40π/4
ω_avg = 10π rad/s

Therefore, the average angular velocity is 10π rad/s.

questions.question: A projectile is launched with horizontal velocity 25 m/s from a height of 80 m. How far horizontally will it travel before hitting the ground? Use g = 9.8 m/s².
questions.explanation:
Given:
Horizontal velocity = 25 m/s
Height = 80 m
g = 9.8 m/s²

First find falling time:
y = (1/2)gt²
80 = 4.9t²
t² = 16.3265
t ≈ 4.04 s

Horizontal motion:
x = vt
x = 25(4.04)
x ≈ 101.0 m

Therefore, the projectile travels approximately 101.0 m horizontally.
